```{r}
# Load Packages
library(terra) # raster handling
library(tidyverse)
library(tmap)
library(spData) # spatial data
library(spDataLarge) # spatial data
library(stars)
```


```{r}
# Load data
depth <- rast("EDS223-HW3/data/depth.tif")
sst_2008 <- rast("EDS223-HW3/data/average_annual_sst_2008.tif")
sst_2009 <- rast("EDS223-HW3/data/average_annual_sst_2009.tif")
sst_2010 <- rast("EDS223-HW3/data/average_annual_sst_2010.tif")
sst_2011 <- rast("EDS223-HW3/data/average_annual_sst_2011.tif")
sst_2012 <- rast("EDS223-HW3/data/average_annual_sst_2012.tif")
wc_regions <- st_read("EDS223-HW3/data/wc_regions_clean.shp")
```

## Process Data

```{r}
# Combine sea surface temperature files

#Check that crs match
print(same.crs(sst_2008, sst_2009))
print(same.crs(sst_2008,sst_2010))
print(same.crs(sst_2008, sst_2011))
print(same.crs(sst_2008, sst_2012))



# Combine files
sst_multiyear <- c(sst_2008, sst_2009, sst_2010, sst_2011, sst_2012)

# Take 4-year mean value of each cell
sst_mean_kel <- mean(sst_multiyear, na.rm = TRUE) 

# Convert to Celsius
sst_mean_c <- sst_mean_kel - 273.15

#Resample the depth data to match the resolution of the SST data using the bilinear method approach
depth_resampled <- resample(depth, sst_mean_c, method = "bilinear")

# Crop depth data to sst data
depth_cropped <- crop(depth_resampled, sst_mean_c)

#Confirm that crs match
same.crs(sst_mean_c, depth_resampled)

crs(sst_mean_c) <- crs(wc_regions)
crs(depth_resampled) <- crs(wc_regions)

#Confirm resolutions, extents, and crs match
print(ext(depth_cropped) == ext(sst_mean_c))
print(same.crs(depth_cropped, sst_mean_c))
print(res(depth_cropped) == res(sst_mean_c))
```


## Find Suitable Locations
To find suitable locations for marine aquaculture, we’ll need to find locations that are suitable in terms of both SST and depth.

reclassify SST and depth data into locations that are suitable for oysters
hint: set suitable values to 1 and unsuitable values to 0
find locations that satisfy both SST and depth conditions


```{r}
# Create reclassification matrix for sst and depth
# Optimal sst range:  11-30°C
# Optimal depth: 0-70 meters below sea level
sst_rcl <- matrix(c(
    0, 11, 0,
    11, 30, 1,
    30, Inf, 0
), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

sst_zones <- classify(sst_mean_c, rcl = sst_rcl)

depth_rcl <- matrix(c(
    -Inf, -70, 0,
    -70, 0, 1,
    0, Inf, 0
), ncol =3, byrow = TRUE)

depth_zones <- classify(depth_cropped, rcl = depth_rcl)


zones_combined <- c(sst_zones, depth_zones)


suitable <- lapp(zones_combined, fun = function(sst, depth) sst*depth)
```

## Determine the most suitable EEZ
We want to determine the total suitable area within each EEZ in order to rank zones by priority. To do so, we need to find the total area of suitable locations within each EEZ.

select suitable cells within West Coast EEZs
find area of grid cells
find the total suitable area within each EEZ
hint: it might be helpful to rasterize the EEZ data

```{r}
# Make EEZ crs equal suitability crs
sf::st_crs(wc_regions) <- terra::crs(suitable)

eez_suitable <- rasterize(wc_regions, suitable, field = 'rgn_id')

# Calculate area using cellsize 
area <- cellSize(suitable, unit = 'km', mask = TRUE)

#Overlay cellsizes to locations
suitable_zones_mask <- mask(area, suitable, maskvalues = 0)

# Calculate the area of suitable zones
zone_area <- zonal(suitable_zones_mask, eez_suitable, fun = "sum", na.rm = TRUE)

zone_table <- as_tibble(zone_area)
```
